# THESE ARE DEFECTS, NOT EXEMPTIONS. Each is a broad catch -- `Exception`,
# receive a `CancellationException` -- with no cancellation clause above it in
# its chain. They are recorded here rather than fixed in the same change that
# added the gate, so that the gate blocks NEW ones from the day it lands instead
# of waiting on a 61-site sweep. The gate prints the outstanding count on every
# run; it does not report the tree as clean.
# #667) each found what the previous one had not looked at, which is the whole
# argument for a gate. Those six are all CLOSED and each was scoped to the tree
# it looked at; none of them tracks this list. #722 does, and it is the issue
# The citation is checked for SHAPE ONLY -- the gate matches `#[0-9]+` and has
# no way to ask whether the number resolves to anything, let alone to anything
# open. `#999999` passes. That limitation is stated here rather than papered
# over: see the header of scripts/check-cancellation-catch-order.sh for why the
# gate does not reach the network to close it. Whoever repoints these rows is
# Columns are those of scripts/cancellation-catch-allowlist.tsv, and the count
# is an exact match against the tree in both directions -- so fixing a site
# fails the gate until its entry is lowered or removed. That is deliberate: it
# is what stops this file becoming the place things go to be forgotten.
# Every reason must cite the tracking issue; the gate enforces that.
# Not yet audited for deliverability, and #722 records the triage rule:

# list should expect to move entries into cancellation-catch-allowlist.tsv with
# a reason rather than treat all 60 as mechanical edits.
